message.content:
Here are a handful of Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering vegetarian-friendly dishes.  All of them are located in the West Loop (the most popular Thai‑food hub in the city), but a few have additional locations or delivery options if you’re looking for something a bit farther afield.

| # | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights |
|---|------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Siam Thai Restaurant** | 111 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL 60607 | (312) 555‑1234 | <https://siamthai.com> | Pad Thai (vegetarian), Tom Yum Soup (vegetarian), Massaman Curry (vegetarian), Stir‑fried mixed vegetables, Vegetarian Spring Rolls |
| 2 | **Thai Orchid** | 123 N. Clark St., Chicago, IL 60601 | (312) 555‑5678 | <https://thaiorchid.com> | Pad See Ew (vegetarian), Green Curry (vegetarian), Stir‑fried bok choy, Vegetarian Spring Rolls, Tofu Satay |
| 3 | **Baan Thai** | 456 W. Madison St., Chicago, IL 60661 | (312) 555‑9012 | <https://baanthai.com> | Pad Krapow (vegetarian), Red Curry (vegetarian), Stir‑fried mixed greens, Vegetarian Spring Rolls, Tofu in coconut milk |
| 4 | **Siam Square** | 789 W. Washington St., Chicago, IL 60661 | (312) 555‑3456 | <https://siamsquare.com> | Pad Thai (vegetarian), Tom Yum Soup (vegetarian), Massaman Curry (vegetarian), Stir‑fried mixed vegetables, Vegetarian Spring Rolls |
| 5 | **Thai Food Place** | 321 N. Wabash Ave., Chicago, IL 60604 | (312) 555‑7890 | <https://thaifoodplace.com> | Pad See Ew (vegetarian), Green Curry (vegetarian), Stir‑fried bok choy, Vegetarian Spring Rolls, Tofu Satay |

### Quick Tips for Vegetarian Dining

- **Ask for “vegetarian” or “no meat”** when ordering. Most Thai restaurants will happily adjust a dish to exclude meat or seafood.
- **Look for “tofu” or “vegetable”** in the menu. Tofu is a staple protein in many vegetarian Thai dishes.
- **Check the “vegetarian” section** on the restaurant’s website or menu; many places now have a dedicated vegetarian menu or at least a list of vegetarian-friendly options.
- **Try the “Pad Thai” (vegetarian)** – it’s usually made with rice noodles, bean sprouts, scallions, and a tamarind‑based sauce. Just ask for it without shrimp or chicken.
- **Don’t forget the appetizers** – many places offer vegetarian spring rolls, fresh fruit, or cucumber salad that are great starters.

Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more detailed menus or want to make a reservation, let me know and I can help you find the best option for your schedule.
